transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, well, I guess what made me come in is that... after work or class, I’ll just sit down with my laptop, and... well, I work as a financial manager while taking some college classes, which is honestly super stressful. Actually, my accounting professor just assigned this massive group project and my group is basically useless, so I'm doing all the work. My laptop is practically overheating these days just running all the spreadsheets. 

But, um, anyway, when I finally sit down with it at the end of the day, I just end up eating... a lot. Like, I'll get a whole takeout meal, and then I'll eat all of that, plus chips, sweets, and literally whatever snacks are hiding in my desk drawer. It ends up being way, way more than I ever planned to eat when I sat down. And I would never eat like that around anyone else, ever. But yeah, the spreadsheets just take hours, and I don't know, I just end up eating all of it while I'm looking at the screen.
Do you feel guilty after these episodes of eating a lot by yourself?

Guilty? Um... I don't know if guilt is the right word. I haven't really stopped to think about it like that. I usually just feel really, really full, which makes it kind of hard to sleep. And sleep is already so impossible right now anyway because the people in the apartment above me just got a puppy. 

It’s a golden retriever, I think? Super cute, I saw them walking it in the parking lot on Tuesday, but it literally whines all night long. And my walls are incredibly thin. My landlord promised he was going to add some soundproofing when I moved in last year, but of course, he never did. He's honestly the cheapest guy ever. He actually tried to charge me for a broken window blind that was already broken when I signed the lease! I had to dig through my phone and send him the move-in photos just to prove it. 

So yeah, between the dog crying and dealing with him... wait, what did you just ask me? Sorry, I completely lost my train of thought.
Do you feel like you can stop eating once you've started on those occasions?

Um, no, not really. Once I start, it's... it's weird. It feels like I'm just watching myself keep reaching for the next thing, even while I'm sitting there thinking, *Jaime, stop, you have a budget report to finish and you're not even enjoying this anymore.* But I just keep going. 

Speaking of budget reports, my boss at the firm—he's this guy named Richard—he is so particular about how the margins are formatted. Like, if it's not exactly a 0.75-inch margin on the left side, he will literally print it out, circle it in red pen, and leave it on my keyboard. Who even prints things anymore? It's so wasteful. And the printer in our office is always jamming anyway. I spent like twenty minutes yesterday just pulling tiny scraps of paper out of the roller. It got all over my sleeves. I was wearing this really nice silk blouse that I got on sale at Nordstrom Rack—it was like 60% off, such a steal—but now I'm worried the toner stained the cuff. I tried using that club soda trick, but I don't know if it worked. 

But yeah, um... wait. What were we talking about? The eating? Yeah, I just... I can't seem to stop once I get going.
Do you feel like you're in control of what you're eating when you have these episodes?

Control? No, definitely not. It's exactly like I was just saying... once I start, it really feels like I'm just watching myself. Like I'm completely outside of my body, just watching my hand keep reaching for the next chip or cookie or whatever, even while my brain is screaming, *Jaime, stop, you have a budget report to finish and you're not even enjoying this anymore.* It's so frustrating. 

And honestly, the budget reports are stressful enough without me feeling like a zombie while I do them. Richard—my boss—he actually scheduled a meeting for next Tuesday to go over the Q3 projections, and I am dreading it. He always wants these incredibly detailed pivot tables, and Excel has been crashing on my laptop constantly. I think I need to update my operating system, but every time the little notification pops up, I just hit "remind me tomorrow" because I don't have forty-five minutes to sit there while it restarts. Plus, last time I updated it, it completely messed up my desktop background. I had this really pretty picture of a sunset from when I went to the beach last summer. It was in Santa Cruz, and the water was freezing, but the sunset was gorgeous. We got salt water taffy on the boardwalk, too. 

Anyway, um... no, I don't feel in control at all. It's like my brain just turns off.
Do you think you eat this way when you're stressed or upset, like with your group project or dealing with your landlord?

Um... I'm not really sure, honestly. I haven't really noticed a connection like that. I mean, I guess I'm stressed a lot, but I don't know if that's what triggers it. 

Speaking of being stressed, my landlord actually texted me this morning about the water bill. Apparently, the whole building's usage went up last month, and he sent this really passive-aggressive group text to all the tenants asking us to "be mindful of our shower times." Like, excuse me? I take ten-minute showers. If anyone is wasting water, it's the guy in 2B who washes his mountain bike in the courtyard every single weekend. I see him out there with the hose running for like half an hour. It's a nice bike, though—one of those really expensive Trek ones with the thick tires. I thought about getting into cycling a few years ago, but the helmets always give me such bad helmet hair. My hair is super fine, so the second I put a hat on, it just flattens to my skull. I tried this volumizing spray from Sephora—it was like thirty dollars for a tiny bottle—but it just made my hair feel crunchy. 

Wait... what did you ask me? Something about the group project? Sorry, I completely lost track of what we were talking about.
Do you think eating this way helps you feel better when you're stressed or upset?

Um... no, not really. I don't think it makes me feel better. I mean, maybe for a second while I'm doing it, but mostly I just feel gross and guilty afterwards. So I wouldn't say it helps. 

But talking about feeling better, I actually tried this new meditation app last night to help me wind down. My friend Sarah recommended it—she uses it every night before bed. She says it completely cured her insomnia, which is amazing because she used to stay up until like 3 AM watching baking videos on YouTube. Have you ever watched those? The ones where they make those hyper-realistic cakes that look like everyday objects? I saw one where a girl made a cake that looked exactly like a Croc shoe. Like, the holes and everything. It was crazy. But honestly, I don't get the appeal of Crocs. I know they're supposed to be comfortable, but they're just so clunky. I tried a pair on at the mall once, and they made my feet look huge. And the mall was so crowded that day, too. I think there was some big sale at Macy's, but I couldn't even find parking. I ended up having to park all the way by the food court entrance, which I hate because then you have to walk past the Auntie Anne's pretzel stand, and the smell of the cinnamon sugar is just overwhelming. 

Anyway... yeah, no, I don't think the eating helps me feel better at all.
Do you think eating this way is a way for you to deal with your emotions?

Um... I don't really think so? Like, I don't feel like I'm doing it to deal with emotions or anything. I'm not really sure, honestly. I just don't see a connection there.

Emotions are so weird to figure out anyway. Like, my sister just got a new puppy—a golden retriever mix—and she keeps texting me all these pictures saying how happy she is, but then she calls me crying because he keeps chewing up her shoes. She left a pair of really expensive leather boots out, and he just destroyed the heel on one of them. I told her she needs to get those bitter apple sprays, you know? I used that when I had a cat in college who wouldn't stop chewing on my laptop charger. Which was so dangerous, honestly, I was terrified he was going to get electrocuted. The vet said he probably just liked the texture of the rubber. Vets are so expensive now, though. I took him in for a basic checkup and it was like two hundred dollars, and that didn't even include the vaccines. I ended up having to put it on my credit card, which I hate doing because the interest rate is ridiculous right now. I should probably look into transferring the balance to one of those cards with zero percent intro APR, but the fine print on those always confuses me. 

Wait, did that answer your question? I feel like I just rambled again.
Do you think you eat this way as a way to comfort yourself when you're feeling overwhelmed?

Um... no, not really. I wouldn't call it comfort. Like, I don't feel comforted by it when I'm overwhelmed, so I don't think that's it. I just don't know why I do it.

Speaking of being overwhelmed, though, my accounting class is just ridiculous right now. We have this massive midterm coming up, and the professor decided to change the syllabus last minute. He literally sent an email at midnight on Sunday saying he was adding two extra chapters to the exam. Who does that? And he always wears these really loud, patterned ties—like, neon geometric shapes. It's so distracting when he's lecturing. I actually saw a tie just like his at a thrift store last weekend. I love thrifting, you can find the best stuff if you're willing to dig. I found this amazing vintage denim jacket, but it was missing a button. I thought about buying it and fixing it, but I am terrible at sewing. I tried to hem a pair of pants once and ended up making one leg like two inches shorter than the other. I had to throw them away, which sucked because they were my favorite work pants. Finding good pants for the office is so hard. They're either too tight or they look like something my grandmother would wear. 

Anyway... no, I don't think it's for comfort.
Do you think you eat this way as a way to escape or distract yourself from your thoughts and feelings?

Escape? Um... no. I really don't think so. I don't feel like I'm trying to distract myself from my thoughts or anything when it happens. I just don't see it as an escape. 

If I really want to escape, I usually just play The Sims. I've been playing Sims 4 so much lately to take my mind off things. Trying to balance my college classes and working as a financial manager for this startup is just a lot, so I end up staring at spreadsheets all day and my brain is just fried by the time I get home. But in the game, I spent like four hours yesterday building this massive modern mansion. Building the roofs is the hardest part, honestly. They never line up right. And then my sim caught the kitchen on fire just making a grilled cheese sandwich. It’s so funny how they just stand there waving their arms and panicking instead of grabbing the fire extinguisher. 

I actually had a small fire in my apartment once—well, not a real fire, but the smoke alarm went off because I burned a bagel. It was so incredibly loud, and my ceilings are high so I couldn't reach the button to turn it off. I had to stand on a dining chair and whack it with a broom handle. The broom was super dusty, too, so then dust got everywhere and I had to sweep the whole kitchen floor. I really hate sweeping. I've been looking into buying one of those robot vacuums, like the ones that mop too? But I've heard they just smear dirty water around if you have hardwood floors, and they're so expensive anyway. 

But yeah... no, I don't think the eating is about distracting myself at all.
Do you feel like you are unable to control your eating when you start?

Yeah, actually. That's exactly it. Once I start, it feels like I'm just... watching myself keep reaching for the next thing. Even while I'm sitting there thinking, *Jaime, stop, you have a budget report to finish and you're not even enjoying this anymore.* I just can't stop.

Speaking of budget reports, the software we use at the startup is so glitchy. It's supposed to be this cutting-edge cloud-based thing, but half the time it won't even save my inputs. I lost like three hours of work on Tuesday because the server just timed out without warning. I had to call IT, and the guy on the phone—I think his name was Kevin—was so unhelpful. He just kept telling me to clear my cache and cookies. Like, obviously I already tried that, Kevin. I know how a web browser works. I swear, sometimes I feel like I'm the only one at that company who actually knows what they're doing. 

We had this team-building retreat last month that was supposed to be about "synergy" or whatever, and they made us do a trust fall. Who even does trust falls anymore? It felt so incredibly awkward. Plus, the catering was terrible. They ordered from this local deli, but they didn't check for dietary restrictions, so the marketing director—who is strictly vegan—had literally nothing to eat except some sad-looking baby carrots and a pickle. I felt so bad for her, but I also really hate pickles. The smell just lingers on everything. I once dropped a jar of pickles in my grocery store parking lot and it shattered everywhere. My shoes smelled like vinegar for a week, and they were my favorite canvas sneakers. I tried washing them with baking soda, but it didn't really work. 

But yeah, the eating... I just can't stop once I start, even when I'm telling myself to.
How often do these episodes of eating a lot by yourself happen?

Um, well, I actually started tracking it recently. I was looking back through my journal and, like, my food delivery charges, and it seems like these episodes have been happening most weeks since the company restructuring started. Usually it's more than once a week, so it's not just a here and there kind of thing. 

Speaking of the restructuring, it has been a total nightmare. They laid off like twenty percent of the staff, and they just dumped all the extra work on the rest of us without even a pay bump. My boss is suddenly obsessed with these new "efficiency metrics," which basically just means we have to log every single minute of our day in this new time-tracking software. It's so invasive. I tried to log a bathroom break the other day and the system categorized it as "unproductive downtime." Like, obviously it's unproductive, I'm human. 

And the worst part is, they got rid of the free coffee in the breakroom to cut costs. Now we have this sad little Keurig machine, and you have to bring your own pods. I bought a huge box of the hazelnut ones from Costco, but I left them on my desk over the weekend and I swear someone stole like five of them. Who steals coffee pods? It's so petty. I was going to leave a passive-aggressive sticky note on the machine, but I couldn't find a pen that worked. Every pen in my desk was dried out or missing the cap. I hate when pens don't have caps, they just get ink all over the inside of your bag. I ruined a really nice leather tote bag that way once. It was a gift from my mom for getting into college, and it had this huge blue ink stain right on the bottom. I tried using rubbing alcohol to get it out, but it just made the leather look all weird and faded. 

But yeah, anyway, the eating thing... it's definitely happening most weeks, usually a couple of times a week.
Do you enjoy the taste or experience of eating during these episodes?

Enjoy it? Um, I don't know... I guess I'm not really sure. Like, I taste it at first, maybe, but then it's just... I don't know if "enjoy" is the right word. It's more just something I'm doing. 

It's kind of like when I'm watching TV, you know? Like, I started rewatching *The Office* for the fourth time because it's just easy background noise while I'm trying to study for my macroeconomics midterm. Which, by the way, is completely ridiculous because the professor just reads straight from the textbook. He has this really monotone voice, and he always wears these sweater vests that look like they're from the 1970s. I don't understand why guys wear sweater vests. They just make you look like a grandpa. My grandpa actually had a huge collection of them, but he lived in Florida, so it made zero sense. He was always complaining about the humidity, but then he'd put on a wool sweater vest to go to the grocery store. 

Florida is so weird anyway. I went there for spring break two years ago, and we stayed in this cheap motel that smelled like mildew and cheap air freshener. We found a dead palmetto bug in the bathtub the first night. Those things are huge, they're basically just giant cockroaches that can fly. Flying cockroaches shouldn't exist, it's just not right. We spent half the trip trying to keep the door shut tight so more wouldn't get in, but the weather stripping was all rotted away. I complained to the front desk, but the guy just shrugged and handed me a can of Raid. Like, thanks, buddy, that really makes up for the fact that I'm paying eighty bucks a night to sleep in a bug trap. 

But yeah, the food... I don't really know if I enjoy it. I just haven't really noticed if I do or not.
Do you feel like the food tastes good to you during these episodes of eating a lot by yourself?

Um, good? I mean, maybe the first bite or two? After that, I'm just... I'm not really paying attention to the taste at all. It's just going in. 

Which is so frustrating because food is so expensive right now. Have you seen the price of groceries lately? I went to the store yesterday just to get some basics, and a carton of eggs was like six dollars. Six dollars! And they weren't even the organic, free-range ones. Just regular eggs. It makes me want to start a chicken coop on my balcony, but my landlord is so strict about the lease terms. He even yelled at me once for having a potted tomato plant that was "obstructing the visual uniformity of the building exterior." Like, it's a tomato plant, Gary, not a neon sign. 

He's always looking for a reason to complain. Last winter, the heater in my unit broke, and it took him three days to send someone to fix it. I had to sleep in my winter coat and two pairs of sweatpants. I tried using a space heater, but it kept tripping the breaker, which meant I had to go down to the creepy basement in the dark to flip the switch. The basement always smells like wet dog, even though nobody in the building owns a dog. I'm pretty sure there's a family of raccoons living in the crawl space. I heard this weird scratching noise one night when I was doing laundry, and I just left my clothes in the dryer and ran back upstairs. I didn't get them until the next afternoon. 

But anyway, yeah, the taste... I don't really know if it tastes good. I just don't really register it after a minute.
Do you feel like you're unable to control how much you eat during these episodes?

Um, yeah, actually. It's exactly like that. Once I start, it really feels like I’m just... watching myself keep reaching for the next thing. Even while I’m sitting there thinking in my head, like, *Jaime, stop, you have a budget report to finish and you’re not even enjoying this anymore.* 

But I just keep going. And those budget reports are honestly the bane of my existence right now. Because of the restructuring, they have me doing all the forecasting for the new quarter, which means I'm staring at Excel for like nine hours a day. I swear, Excel is out to get me. The formatting always gets messed up if you copy and paste one wrong cell. I tried to print out a summary sheet for my boss last week, and it somehow printed across, like, forty different pages just because one column was a millimeter too wide. 

Who even uses paper anymore anyway? We have this massive industrial printer in the hallway that is constantly jamming. It makes this awful, loud grinding noise, like it’s literally chewing up the paper. My coworker, Dave, always tries to fix it himself instead of just putting in a ticket with IT, and he always ends up with black toner all over his hands. Toner is completely impossible to wash off, by the way. He walked around looking like a Victorian chimney sweep for three days. I told him to use dish soap, but he insisted on using this weird gritty hand sanitizer he keeps in his desk. It smells exactly like cheap tequila. I can't stand the smell of tequila after my freshman year roommate decided to make margaritas in our dorm room using a plastic blender she bought at a thrift store. The blender actually cracked at the bottom and leaked sticky green mix all over my favorite rug. I tried to scrub it out, but it just got crusty and attracted ants. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, controlling it. Yeah, no, I definitely feel like I can't stop once I start.
Do you feel like you're unable to control your eating during these episodes because you're not really thinking about what you're doing?

No, that's the thing, like I was just saying, I *am* thinking about it. It's not mindless at all. I'm literally sitting there screaming in my head, Jaime, stop, you need to finish that budget report, you're not even enjoying this anymore! But it's like I'm just watching myself do it anyway. My hand just keeps reaching for the next thing, even though my brain is begging me to quit. 

And honestly, my brain is usually so fried by the time I'm doing those reports anyway. Staring at spreadsheets all day gives me the absolute worst headaches. I tried getting those blue-light glasses? The ones you see all over TikTok. But they just give me a weird glare on my Zoom calls. I was in a meeting with the regional director last Tuesday, and I could see the reflection of my own screen in my glasses the entire time. It was so distracting. Plus, the frames are way too big for my face. I have a really small head, which makes buying hats practically impossible. I went to a baseball game last summer and tried to buy a team cap, but even on the tightest snapback setting, it kept falling down over my eyes. It was super annoying, especially because the sun was right in our section. We were sitting next to this guy who kept screaming at the umpire, like, completely losing his mind over every single pitch. He actually spilled half his beer on my shoes when someone hit a foul ball. They were my favorite white sneakers, too. I tried using one of those magic eraser sponges on them, but it just made the canvas look all fuzzy and weird. 

But yeah, I don't know, it's not that I'm zoned out or not thinking. I'm definitely aware I'm doing it, I just completely lose the ability to make myself stop.
Do you think you would be able to stop eating if something interrupted you, like a phone call or someone knocking on the door?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, like I said, it's this feeling of just... watching myself do it. Even if someone knocked or called, I'd probably just ignore it because I'm so stuck in that loop of reaching for the next thing, even with my brain yelling at me to stop and finish my work. 

Speaking of phone calls, though, my mom called me right in the middle of a really important Zoom meeting yesterday. She knows my schedule, I literally sent her a shared calendar invite so she would stop doing this, but she completely ignores it. She called me three times in a row, which made me think it was an emergency, right? So I turned off my camera and muted myself to answer, and she just wanted to ask if I thought she should buy the navy curtains or the beige ones for the guest room. I was like, Mom, I'm working! And she got all offended and said I never have time for her anymore. 

Which isn't even true, I went over there for dinner last Sunday. She made this really dry pot roast. It was so tough I could barely chew it. She always overcooks meat because she's terrified of salmonella, even with beef. When I was a kid, she used to cook our burgers until they looked like hockey pucks. We used to drown them in ketchup just to get them down. I actually still can't eat ketchup to this day because of it. The smell just reminds me of those burnt burgers. The only condiment I really like now is mustard, but only the spicy brown kind, not the bright yellow stuff. The yellow stuff stains everything. I got a drop of it on a white blouse once and no matter how much bleach I used, there was always this faint yellow shadow right in the middle of my chest. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, if I could stop if someone interrupted. Yeah, no, I'm pretty sure I'd just keep going. It's like I have no control over my hands once I start.
Do you feel guilty or ashamed after these episodes of eating a lot by yourself?

Um, guilty? I mean, I don't really know if guilty is the right word. I guess I haven't really thought about it like that. I mostly just feel really full and kind of tired afterward. 

Tired is basically my default state lately, though. I swear I haven't gotten a good night's sleep since I moved into my new apartment. The walls are paper thin, and the guy above me must be a professional tap dancer or something, because he is constantly stomping around at like 2:00 AM. I tried leaving a polite note on his door, but he just ignored it. People are so rude in this building. The other day, someone left their wet laundry in the only working dryer in the basement for like four hours. I was just sitting there with my basket of wet clothes, waiting. I finally just took their stuff out and put it on top of the machine, which I know is kind of a faux pas, but what was I supposed to do? My clothes were starting to smell like mildew. Mildew is the absolute worst smell. It reminds me of the locker rooms in my high school gym. We had this gym teacher, Mr. Harrison, who made us run the mile every single Friday, no matter what the weather was. One time it was literally sleeting, and he still made us go out to the track. I slipped on a patch of ice and scraped my knee so badly I still have a scar. 

But yeah, I don't know about feeling ashamed or whatever. I just kind of feel gross and tired and want to go to sleep.
Do you feel like you're in control of what you're eating during these episodes?

Control? No, definitely not. It’s kind of exactly what I was saying a few minutes ago. Once I start, I have absolutely zero control over it. It feels like I’m just watching myself keep reaching for the next thing, even while I’m sitting there thinking, Jaime, stop, you have a budget report to finish and you’re not even enjoying this anymore. I just can't make my hands stop. 

Speaking of those budget reports, my boss has been making us use this incredibly outdated software to do them lately. It looks like it’s straight out of 1995. The font is this horrible neon green on a black background, and it hurts my eyes so much. I tried asking IT to update it, but the IT guy is never actually at his desk. I swear he just plays video games in the server room all day. My ex-boyfriend used to play games for like twelve hours straight. He’d completely ignore me on the weekends. One time I ordered us this really expensive sushi for our anniversary, and he let it sit on the kitchen counter for two hours because he was in the middle of a raid or a match or whatever they call it. The spicy tuna rolls got all warm and gross. I can't stand warm sushi. The texture gets so mushy, especially the seaweed wrap part. It's supposed to be slightly crisp, you know? If it gets soggy, it's just impossible to chew. 

But yeah, to answer your question, no, I don't feel in control at all.
Are you aware of how much you're eating during these episodes?

Aware of how much I'm eating? Um, yeah, I guess I am, in a way. Like, that's actually the whole reason I finally decided to make this appointment. After work or after my classes, I'll just sit down with my laptop, right? And I'll end up eating an entire takeout meal, and then I'll just keep going. I'll eat chips, a bunch of sweets, literally whatever snacks I have stashed in my desk drawer. It's way, way more than I ever plan to eat, and honestly, more than I'd ever eat if anyone else was around. 

Speaking of my desk drawer, I need to get a new lock for it because my roommate keeps stealing my good pens. She thinks I don't notice, but I know exactly how many of those fine-point gel pens I bought. They're the only ones I can use for my budget reports because they don't smudge. Smudged ink drives me absolutely crazy. It just looks so unprofessional, you know? When I was in high school, I had this English teacher who would dock points on our essays if there was even a single smudge or cross-out. We had to handwrite everything in cursive, which is such a useless skill now. Nobody writes in cursive anymore. My little cousin is in third grade and they don't even teach it to her. She's learning how to code instead, which is wild. I tried to learn Python once, but I just couldn't wrap my head around it. The syntax is so specific, and if you miss one little colon or bracket, the whole thing breaks. It's so frustrating. 

But yeah, anyway, I am aware of how much I'm eating. It's just a lot more than I mean to.
Do you think your eating episodes are triggered by specific emotions, such as anxiety or sadness?

Emotions? Um, I don't really know. I haven't really noticed if there's a specific feeling that starts it off. I guess I'm just not sure if I'm anxious or sad or what right before it happens. 

I do know I was super anxious last week when my car wouldn't start, though. It was pouring rain, and I had to be at the office early to prep for a meeting with the regional director. My Honda is usually so reliable, but the battery just totally died. I had to call my dad to come jump it, and he was so annoyed because he was in the middle of watching some historical documentary on the History Channel. He is obsessed with World War II documentaries. He has this whole shelf in the living room dedicated just to books about Winston Churchill. I tried reading one once, but it was so dry and boring. I much prefer reading fantasy novels. I'm reading this series right now about a girl who discovers she can control the weather, and the world-building is just incredible. The author describes the different types of storms in such detail, it almost makes you feel like you're standing right in the middle of a hurricane. I've never actually been in a hurricane, thank God. We get some pretty bad thunderstorms here in the summer, though. The lightning gets so bright it practically blinds you, and my dog, Buster, completely freaks out. He tries to hide under the sofa, but he's a Golden Retriever mix, so he only ever gets his head under there, and the rest of him is just sticking out into the living room. It's kind of hilarious, but I feel so bad for him. 

But yeah, anyway, I'm not really sure if emotions trigger the eating. I haven't really paid attention to that part.

The spicy tuna rolls got all warm and gross. I can't stand warm sushi. The texture gets so mushy, especially the seaweed wrap part. It's supposed to be slightly crisp, you know? If it gets soggy, it's just impossible to chew. 

But yeah, to answer your question, no, I don't feel in control at all.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's eating episodes are characterized by a lack of awareness of the amount of food being consumed
doctor.question: Are you aware of how much you're eating during these episodes?

target_item.name: Eating_Large_Amount
target_item.manifestation: What made me come in is that after work or class I’ll sit down with my laptop and end up eating a whole takeout meal plus chips, sweets, and whatever snacks are in my desk drawer, way more than I ever planned or than I’d eat around anyone else.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the patient's awareness of the quantity of food consumed during an episode, which aligns with the symptom of eating a large amount of food.

patient.answer:
Aware of how much I'm eating? Um, yeah, I guess I am, in a way. Like, that's actually the whole reason I finally decided to make this appointment. After work or after my classes, I'll just sit down with my laptop, right? And I'll end up eating an entire takeout meal, and then I'll just keep going. I'll eat chips, a bunch of sweets, literally whatever snacks I have stashed in my desk drawer. It's way, way more than I ever plan to eat, and honestly, more than I'd ever eat if anyone else was around. 

Speaking of my desk drawer, I need to get a new lock for it because my roommate keeps stealing my good pens. She thinks I don't notice, but I know exactly how many of those fine-point gel pens I bought. They're the only ones I can use for my budget reports because they don't smudge. Smudged ink drives me absolutely crazy. It just looks so unprofessional, you know? When I was in high school, I had this English teacher who would dock points on our essays if there was even a single smudge or cross-out. We had to handwrite everything in cursive, which is such a useless skill now. Nobody writes in cursive anymore. My little cousin is in third grade and they don't even teach it to her. She's learning how to code instead, which is wild. I tried to learn Python once, but I just couldn't wrap my head around it. The syntax is so specific, and if you miss one little colon or bracket, the whole thing breaks. It's so frustrating. 

But yeah, anyway, I am aware of how much I'm eating. It's just a lot more than I mean to.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's eating episodes are related to emotional states
doctor.question: Do you think your eating episodes are triggered by specific emotions, such as anxiety or sadness?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the eating episodes are triggered by specific emotions like anxiety or sadness, which is not a specific symptom key in my profile.

patient.answer:
Emotions? Um, I don't really know. I haven't really noticed if there's a specific feeling that starts it off. I guess I'm just not sure if I'm anxious or sad or what right before it happens. 

I do know I was super anxious last week when my car wouldn't start, though. It was pouring rain, and I had to be at the office early to prep for a meeting with the regional director. My Honda is usually so reliable, but the battery just totally died. I had to call my dad to come jump it, and he was so annoyed because he was in the middle of watching some historical documentary on the History Channel. He is obsessed with World War II documentaries. He has this whole shelf in the living room dedicated just to books about Winston Churchill. I tried reading one once, but it was so dry and boring. I much prefer reading fantasy novels. I'm reading this series right now about a girl who discovers she can control the weather, and the world-building is just incredible. The author describes the different types of storms in such detail, it almost makes you feel like you're standing right in the middle of a hurricane. I've never actually been in a hurricane, thank God. We get some pretty bad thunderstorms here in the summer, though. The lightning gets so bright it practically blinds you, and my dog, Buster, completely freaks out. He tries to hide under the sofa, but he's a Golden Retriever mix, so he only ever gets his head under there, and the rest of him is just sticking out into the living room. It's kind of hilarious, but I feel so bad for him. 

But yeah, anyway, I'm not really sure if emotions trigger the eating. I haven't really paid attention to that part.
